transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-01-12 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Evan (CSM), Marcus (Cerulean), Sofia, Ravi, Lena, Akash

Summary:
Quick QBR-style health check — usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents last quarter, and roadmap alignment for upcoming feature launch. Discussed pilot options (hosted vs dedicated), security requirements, and an initial benchmarking plan.

Topics covered:
- Recent usage patterns & unexpected peaks
- Cost anomalies in December billing
- p95/p99 latency targets for product launch (50ms target for short prompts seems optimistic)
- Private deployment constraints (VPC + KMS) and SOC2 scope
- Next steps: bench, pricing TCO, security artifacts, pilot kickoff

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for making time. we'll do a quick health check and then focus on the upcoming launch readiness. is that fine?
[00:08] Marcus: yep that works. short heads up, December spiked more than we expected so want to understand root cause and options to control spend.
[00:15] Priya: oh got it, can you give a sense, like was it request volume or bigger contexts?
[00:20] Marcus: volume mainly, but also more long-form sessions — some calls had 2k token contexts which amplified cost.
[00:27] Sofia: and that coincided with a heavy A/B test, so the traffic pattern was unusual. we didn't throttle as aggressively as usual.
[00:33] Evan: thanks. we pulled the bill and saw the same; a few high-cardinality users plus longer sequences. we can show the token-level breakdown after the call.
[00:40] Ravi: real quick, do you have recommendations — like should we switch to dedicated for the launch or tune batching and caching?
[00:46] Priya: depends on the SLA you need. Dedicated gives predictability and often better p95, but hosted with aggressive prefix caching and quantized model variants can save a lot if you don't need strict isolation.
[00:58] Lena: security note — we will need KMS integration and full audit logs. SOC2 is table stakes. on-prem is not required but VPC + customer-managed keys are.
[01:08] Jordan: that's helpful. Evan, can you walk through the reliability incidents in Q4?
[01:12] Evan: sure. we had two incidents: one was a model snapshot misroute that caused elevated error rates for ~12 minutes on Dec 3, and another was a burst-induced queue saturation on Dec 19 that bumped tail latency. both were mitigated by our fallback policy to a smaller model variant.
[01:27] Marcus: that fallback worked but we observed some user-facing quality degradation, so the product team flagged it.
[01:33] Priya: right, there's a tradeoff — fallback helps availability but can change model outputs. we can set canary rules to preferentially route critical customers to reserved capacity.
[01:42] Akash: curious — is there an autoscale configuration you recommend for sudden spikes? we run KEDA for other workloads.
[01:48] Priya: for Redwood Dedicated we suggest a two-tier buffer: reserved baseline + burst pool. autoscale policies can be time-windowed to avoid thrash.
[01:55] Ravi: about latency — your offering lists 30-50ms for some variants, is that realistic for our 512-token prompts?
[02:02] Priya: 30ms is optimistic for very small prompts/non-cryptic models. for 512 tokens p95 on A100-class hosts we'd expect 80-120ms depending on model and KV cache hit rates. caching and batching change the effective cost per token.
[02:14] Marcus: cost-wise, do you have a quick TCO example for heavy read workloads?
[02:19] Jordan: yes, we'll send a sample TCO spreadsheet. quick verbal: hosted is lower up-front but variable; dedicated reduces unit cost at scale but needs commitment. with prefix caching you can often get 30-50% token reduction on repeat flows.
[02:34] Sofia: can Redwood provide a simulated run with our payloads? we want to see p95 and token burn with real prompts.
[02:41] Priya: absolutely. if you can share representative payloads and traffic shape, we'll run a 48-hour bench and return p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates.
[02:49] Lena: and security please share the SOC2 package and KMS integration docs; also confirm retention windows and deletion APIs.
[02:57] Evan: noted — we'll send links. quick question for Cerulean: what's the timeline for the feature launch again?
[03:04] Marcus: aiming for late February with a soft beta mid-February. so we'd like a pilot in Jan.
[03:09] Jordan: good we can do bench + security review this month and then a pilot kickoff week of Jan 26.
[03:15] Akash: any red flags for on-prem? we've been experimenting but likely do VPC first.
[03:20] Priya: VPC + customer-managed KMS is straightforward, on-prem is more involved — requires packaging and air-gapped support. we can scope it but it moves the timeline.
[03:30] Marcus: also curious about observability — does the console give token-level cost by route? we need to attribute spend to features.
[03:36] Evan: yes, token-level attribution and per-route dashboards are available; we'll share screenshots and enable a demo account so you can see the console.
[03:44] Ravi: what about model rollouts? we can't have a rollout break behavior in prod.
[03:48] Priya: rollouts support canary and automatic fallback; you can pin versions by route. plus we have an eval hook to run your prompt set pre-rollout to detect regressions.
[03:57] Marcus: any competitors you see customers choosing for similar use cases?
[04:01] Jordan: customers look at self-host (for IRL control), Vertex for tight GCP integration, and Lambda for GPU ops. we discussed tradeoffs earlier.
[04:09] Sofia: ok can we get a pricing delta table: hosted vs dedicated vs hybrid for our expected Q1 volumes?
[04:14] Jordan: yes — we'll include that in the TCO.
[04:17] Evan: action items recap — Priya bench, Evan share console and security links, Marcus provide payloads/traces, Lena confirm audit scope.
[04:25] Marcus: i'll get the traces and payloads by monday.
[04:28] Lena: security artifacts by Thursday, will confirm encryption constraints.
[04:32] Jordan: great, we'll follow up with invites for the bench kickoff and pilot kickoff. thanks everyone.
[04:36] Sofia: thanks all, good meeting.

Post-meeting notes (auto):
- Redwood recommended pilot plan: 48h bench -> 2-week pilot on hosted with burst to dedicated if needed.
- Primary risk: long-context sessions driving token burn; mitigation: prefix/KV caching + model quantization and canary reserved capacity.
- Decision drivers for Cerulean: cost predictability (favor dedicated at scale), security (VPC + KMS), and launch timeline (beta mid-Feb).

End of transcript.
